title: Include Visits with Zero Transactions
learning_objective: Learn why LEFT JOIN is needed when missing matches still matter.

tutorial.explanation: INNER JOIN drops visits with no transactions. LEFT JOIN keeps every visit and fills transaction columns with NULL when no match exists.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT v.visit_id, COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS transaction_count FROM visits v LEFT JOIN transactions t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id GROUP BY v.visit_id;
tutorial.mental_model: Start from the table whose rows must survive. Then LEFT JOIN optional details onto it.

guided_example.prompt: Count transactions for every visit, including zero-transaction visits.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT v.visit_id, COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS transaction_count FROM visits v LEFT JOIN transactions t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id GROUP BY v.visit_id;
guided_example.explanation: COUNT(t.transaction_id) counts only matched transaction ids. Visits without matches become 0.

practice.prompt: Return visit_id for visits with zero transactions.
practice.expected_query: SELECT v.visit_id FROM visits v LEFT JOIN transactions t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id GROUP BY v.visit_id HAVING COUNT(t.transaction_id) = 0;
